claims.statement: URE describes a guarantee of origin as the sole document proving to a final customer that the specified energy quantity was produced from renewable sources, and states that it carries no property rights.
Guarantees are electronic, individually identified, valid for twelve months after production, and must be cancelled or expire under controlled registry rules.

TGE issues final-customer confirmation at the seller-owner's request and in April 2026 added bulk transaction handling plus a registry marketplace, directly addressing aggregation and transaction workflow.

Axpo says its nearly 40000 Polish SME customers receive renewable-origin coverage and that it introduced green electricity without additional or hidden fees; Energa's 2026 terms provide collective GO purchase and cancellation for covered customers.
AIB reported that Poland had a functioning national system but no AIB Hub connection and no membership timeline, limiting assumptions about standardized cross-border transfer.

EU consumer law restricts unsubstantiated generic environmental claims and claims that overstate a benefit for an entire product or business, so a GO evidence export cannot safely authorize broad green claims.

contrary_evidence: Axpo already includes renewable-origin coverage for a large SME base without an added fee, sharply challenging the proposed standalone subscription.
Energa already pools GO purchasing and cancellation across customers.
TGE's 2026 registry release includes bulk transactions and a marketplace, reducing the value of a separate pooled procurement interface.
Guarantees prove energy attributes but do not carry property rights or establish physical delivery from a chosen renewable plant.
Poland remained outside the AIB Hub in the reviewed report, complicating cross-border sourcing and interoperability assumptions.
Green-claims rules require specific, supportable wording; the service cannot turn certificate ownership into unrestricted ESG or product claims.

economics.acquisition_route: Secure one registry-capable adviser or supplier willing to provide ten anonymized invoice and cancellation cases, then sell through its portfolio; family installer referrals are only a secondary test channel.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: At a revised 2 PLN per MWh administration yield, 1 TWh produces 2m PLN revenue; 40% EBITDA is 800000 PLN and a 6x multiple is 4.8m PLN enterprise value before subscriptions. Exceeding 5m PLN founder net worth therefore needs more than 1 TWh, meaningful subscription revenue, high ownership, and durable channel control, none of which is validated against bundled incumbents.
economics.founder_time: 10-15 hours weekly for a non-custodial pilot if all registry actions, sourcing, cancellation, and regulated advice remain with the partner.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Software reconciliation could exceed 75% gross margin after partner fees at scale, but manual exception review, registry operations, support, and partner share are unknown and may dominate small accounts.
economics.payback: Not underwritten. At 50000 PLN setup capital, fourteen SMEs paying 300 PLN monthly for one year produce about 50400 PLN revenue before partner share and support; bundled free alternatives make that conversion assumption unvalidated.
economics.pricing: The original 800-2000 PLN monthly SME price is contradicted by bundled supplier offers. Test 150-600 PLN monthly per SME or a 10000-30000 PLN annual wholesale partner licence, plus 2-5 PLN per MWh only for documented exception handling; certificate cost remains pass-through.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual disclosure, monthly invoices, expiry, and recurring customer requests support repeat use, but TGE bulk processing and supplier-bundled cancellation can absorb the workflow.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Normalized invoice formats, customer evidence templates, exception history, and partner operating data can improve reconciliation and audit readiness
fingerprint.customer: Polish energy advisers, electricity suppliers, and supply-chain reporting firms serving SMEs that need buyer-specific renewable-origin evidence
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embed with energy advisers, licensed suppliers, accountants, renewable installers, and supply-chain reporting platforms rather than acquire SMEs one by one
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Non-custodial invoice reconciliation, allocation ledger, expiry alerts, registry-confirmation attachment, and constrained evidence export; all GO purchase, holding, transfer, and cancellation stays with an authorised counterparty
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A channel partner pays a wholesale software licence or the SME pays a modest workspace fee when a buyer-specific evidence pack is issued after registry-confirmed cancellation
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An SME or its customer requests auditable renewable-electricity evidence linked to a reporting period and consumption record

founder_fit: Invoice reconciliation, exception detection, and evidence exports fit the founder's data and automation strengths.
The renewable-energy context and family installer network can support a small referral test.
A non-custodial partner model is capital-light and avoids inventory, trading exposure, and a public brand.
Winning energy suppliers and advisers still requires regulated-market credibility and concentrated B2B selling.
risks: Unlicensed trading, brokerage, or certificate custody
Misleading green claims or double counting
Concentration in a small number of registry-capable partners
Low willingness to pay for evidence already bundled with electricity supply

structure.control_point: The reconciliation record joining metered consumption, a named final customer, unique certificate attributes, and registry-confirmed cancellation
structure.critical_dependency: A registry-capable counterparty willing to issue buyer-specific confirmation and a contract that keeps the startup outside energy trading, certificate custody, and misleading-claims scope

thesis: Provide invoice-to-guarantee reconciliation, buyer-specific evidence exports, expiry controls, and claims guardrails through an energy adviser, supplier, or other registry-capable counterparty. Keep certificate custody, trading, and cancellation with that partner and describe guarantees only as energy-origin evidence, not physical renewable delivery. The need for auditable allocation is real, but TGE now supports bulk transactions and a marketplace, Polish suppliers already bundle collective cancellation for SMEs, and one large incumbent says renewable-origin coverage is included without extra fees, making the original standalone subscription and pooled-procurement economics doubtful.
title: SME Guarantee-of-Origin Reconciliation Add-On
uncertainties: Which entities can hold, transfer, and request cancellation in the current Polish registry and on whose behalf
Whether a non-custodial mandate or software layer triggers energy-trading, brokerage, or other licensing duties
Availability of buyer-named or site-level confirmations through partner workflows
Actual GO and registry fee schedule, partner split, and minimum economical volume
SME willingness to pay when suppliers bundle renewable-origin coverage
Whether supply-chain customers require granular invoice allocation beyond existing supplier certificates
Poland's timing and terms for AIB Hub connection
Data access and API support in the TGE registry
